answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price trust like a river delta: every new identity starts as a thin willow shoot with almost no flow, and its channel only widens after verified work over time. Cheap throwaway identities stay narrow streams that cannot carry large payments, while long-lived agents earn wider deltas. An attacker would need to nurture thousands of willow shoots for months to match one trusted agent, raising the cost of faking volume above any profit.
